title: Error Handling and Debugging
description: Understanding error handling techniques and debugging tools in Node.js applications to write more robust code.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used in JavaScript to handle exceptions?
quiz.explanation: The try-catch block is used to handle exceptions in JavaScript.

quiz.question: What function is used to explicitly raise an error in Node.js?
quiz.explanation: The throw statement is used to throw an exception.

quiz.question: Which Node.js module can be used for debugging applications?
quiz.explanation: The `--inspect` flag enables debugging using Chrome DevTools or other tools.

quiz.question: What will happen if an error is not caught in a Node.js application?
quiz.explanation: Uncaught exceptions typically cause the Node.js application to terminate.

quiz.question: How can asynchronous errors be handled in Node.js?
quiz.explanation: Callbacks in Node.js often use the first argument as an error object for handling async errors.

quiz.question: Which method is used to print debugging information to the console?
quiz.explanation: `console.log()` outputs messages to the console for debugging purposes.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the 'finally' block in a try-catch-finally statement?
options: To execute code regardless of whether an error occurred or not
quiz.correctAnswer: To execute code regardless of whether an error occurred or not
quiz.explanation: The finally block runs after try and catch, no matter the outcome.

quiz.question: Which tool integrates with Node.js for visual debugging?
quiz.explanation: Chrome DevTools can connect to Node.js using the --inspect flag for debugging.

quiz.question: What does the 'uncaughtException' event in Node.js do?
options: It is emitted when an exception bubbles all the way back to the event loop
quiz.correctAnswer: It is emitted when an exception bubbles all the way back to the event loop
quiz.explanation: This event can be used to log and clean up before exiting the process.

quiz.question: Why is it important to handle errors in Node.js applications?
options: To prevent application crashes and ensure stability
quiz.correctAnswer: To prevent application crashes and ensure stability
quiz.explanation: Proper error handling improves application reliability and user experience.
